title: Abstract Priorities, Concrete Rewards: How Stated Preferences Relate to What People Reward in AI Responses
abstract: arXiv:2610.30763v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI assistants built on large language models (LLMs) are trained on human feedback and increasingly personalized to users' stated preferences. Yet how closely these preferences reflect what people reward in responses remains unclear. We compare stated and revealed preferences in the public PRISM dataset, in which 1,396 participants reported how much seven response attributes mattered to them and then rated 29,347 responses from 21 LLMs. Among responses to the same prompt, features the survey never asked about, such as response length, formatting and refusal language, were at least as strongly associated with ratings as text proxies of the surveyed attributes. Whether stated priorities matched ratings depended on how attributes were measured: participants who prioritized an attribute favoured responses from models that others perceived as strong on it, but not responses that scored higher on text proxies for it. translated_title: 抽象的优先级，具体的奖励：陈述性偏好与人们在AI回复中实际奖励内容的关系
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）构建的AI助手通过人类反馈进行训练，并日益根据用户陈述的偏好进行个性化定制。然而，这些偏好与人们在回复中实际奖励的内容之间的吻合程度仍不清楚。我们在公开的PRISM数据集中比较了陈述性偏好与显示性偏好：在该数据集中，1,396名参与者报告了七个回复属性对他们的重要程度，随后对来自21个大语言模型的29,347条回复进行了评分。在针对同一提示词的回复中，问卷从未询问过的特征——如回复长度、格式和拒绝语言——与评分的关联强度至少不亚于所调查属性的文本代理指标。陈述的优先级是否与评分相符，取决于属性的测量方式：重视某一属性的参与者更偏好其他用户认为在该属性上表现出色的模型所产生的回复，而非在相应文本代理指标上得分更高的回复。书面反馈则更为……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究基于PRISM数据集发现，人们对AI回复的评分受回复长度、格式、拒绝语言等未被直接询问的具体特征的影响不亚于被调查的属性，且陈述的偏好只有在模型整体感知层面（而非文本指标层面）才与实际奖励行为一致，表明陈述性偏好未必反映人们真正奖励的内容。
en_tdlr: Analyzing the PRISM dataset, this study finds that users' ratings of AI responses are at least as strongly driven by unasked-about features such as length, formatting, and refusal language as by surveyed attributes, and that stated priorities align with actual rewards only at the level of perceived model strengths rather than textual measures.
